name: From Cost Barriers to Circular Assets: Policy & Operational Models for EV Battery Recycling
description: As electric vehicles and stationary energy storage units become more common, managing end-of-life batteries presents direct operational and financial challenges. In many regions, salvage yards and local dismantlers face high processing and transport fees for large format batteries, leaving them hesitant to accept battery systems or entire vehicles without clear cost-effective management pathways. Join industry speakers for a practical discussion on how state policy, processing innovations, and industry advocacy are coming together to address these cost barriers and keep valuable critical minerals in circulation. This session will explore Colorado’s landmark legislation that brought automakers, recyclers, and auto dismantlers into a balanced framework, Cirba Solutions' operational approaches to EV battery processing economics and scale, and the Recycled Materials Association’s (ReMA) work to promote safe EV and lithium-ion battery recycling through advocacy, safety training, and public education.

name: Dhonielle Clayton: "The Paragon Games"
description:
Return to the world of the Marvellers and Conjurors in this fourth book of the instant New York Times and #1 Indie Bestselling fantasy series. Year Four at the global magic school in the sky is back in session in The Paragon Games.

 

As Ella and Jason return for Year Four at the Arcanum training institute, the world is in turmoil. The Marvellian and Conjure communities have been shattered by learning the truth of the shocking death of the school's Conjure architect. Brigit is still missing. Masterji Thakur is gone. Worst of all, the villainous Gia Trivelino brews a nefarious plot to recreate monstrous marvels. And the key to powering her plan, a stockpile of twilight stars, has been stolen from the Conjure Underworld.

 

As violence and political upheaval erupt, and Ella and Jason search for Brigit, the pair get selected to participate in the year-long Paragon Games. The prize for the winner: a wish granted. With Ella being tugged in a dozen directions, she must compete in the games, beat Gia to locating the stolen twilight stars, and help build a bridge between two communities on the precipice of war.

 

About the Author:

Dhonielle Clayton is a New York Times bestselling author of The Conjureverse series, The Belles series, Shattered Midnight, co-author of Blackout, Whiteout, The Rumor Game, and of the Tiny Pretty Things duology, a Netflix original series. She hails from the Washington, D.C. suburbs on the Maryland side. She taught secondary school for several years, and is a former elementary and middle school librarian. She is COO of the non-profit We Need Diverse Books.  She’s an avid traveler, and always on the hunt for magic and mischief.

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: The Life of Frankenstein
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“The Life of Frankenstein,”** on the birth, evolution and impact of a tale of man-made monstrosity, with Bernard Welt, an emeritus professor of arts and humanities at George Washington University who frequently lectures on Frankenstein in literature, cinema, and culture.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-life-of-frankenstein](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-life-of-frankenstein) .]

Guillermo del Toro’s lush and lovingly produced film adaptation of Mary Shelley’s 1818 novel *Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus* is just the latest of many iterations of the story to capture the public’s imagination. People have watched Victor Frankenstein give life to his monster in numerous films, on television, and on stage, and even perform “Putting on the Ritz” with him thanks to the comic genius of Mel Brooks.

Mary Shelley did not just tell a tale. She spawned the modern genre of speculative fiction and gave rise to a myth that would crop up in debates over nature versus nurture and other matters. Even today it stokes anxieties over the potential impacts of robotics, artificial intelligence, and genetic engineering, by evoking the image of a monster turning on its progenitor.

Come gain a new appreciation of Mary Shelley’s creation with the help of Dr. Bernard Welt, who has studied the relationship between nightmares and the horror genre and is the author of *Mythomania: Fantasies, Fables, and Sheer Lies in Contemporary American Popular Art.*

Dr. Welt will start by telling a literary origin story almost as famous as Frankenstein itself, of how an 18-year-old Shelley started writing Frankenstein in 1816 while staying in a villa on Lake Geneva with two of her era’s leading poets, Lord Byron and Percy Bysshe Shelley, her lover. Housebound by foul weather, the three read Gothic tales of ghosts and monsters and challenged each other to produce something even more terrifying. Mary dreamed up a story of a man who defied death by creating a living being out of scraps of deceased men harvested from graveyards and anatomy labs.

The resulting novel, *Frankenstein*, published anonymously in 1818, would by that century’s end become a touchstone in philosophical discourse on the nature of humanity and in political discussions of imperialism and populism. By the 21st century, Mary Shelley (as she became) had earned a more significant place in the literary canon than Byron and her husband Shelley.

We will examine how this grisly tale became a landmark of modern thought and look at the part played by numerous film adaptations from the first years of cinema to the present day. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID. Bar doors open at 5 pm. The talk starts at 6:30.)

Image: From a Theodor von Holst engraving in an 1831 edition of Frankenstein published by Colburn and Bentley of London.

name: Riley Black: "Tyrant Lizard Queen"
description:
From the author of the beloved The Last Days of the Dinosaurs, an imaginative celebration of T. rex from hatching to adulthood

 

Tyrannosaurus rex is a prehistoric celebrity. Exceeding 40 feet in length and weighing over 9 tons, the largest individuals of this dinosaurian species were intimidating predators capable of crushing bone and consuming more than a hundred pounds of flesh in a bite. But the last of the tyrant dinosaurs had a life beyond ripping and tearing. More than 66 million years ago, T. rex courted each other, nested, watched over their offspring, slept, drank, and explored ancient floodplains inhabited by a fantastic cast of impressive dinosaurs like the huge long-neck Alamosaurus and burly, three-horned Torosaurus. For the first time, the life story of this impressive, sensitive predator is told as if you were there to watch it unfold.

 

In her latest prehistoric nature walk, bestselling and award-winning author Riley Black follows the life of plucky T. rex Snaggletooth from the time she hatches through her tumultuous adulthood. The prehistoric forest Snag emerges into is full of danger, and yet, as Riley weaves the latest fossil discoveries into the story, the carnivorous dinosaur survives to play, court, fight, sleep, nest, and more as she grows up in Cretaceous North America. She tussles with rival tyrannosaurs, hunts for delectable prey, and finds soft moments of connection in the forest. Even the most die-hard dinosaur fan will come away with a new perspective and appreciation for the Tyrant Lizard Queen.

 

Riley Black will be joined in conversation by WYPR's Senior News Analyst Tom Hall. 

 

About the Author: 

RILEY BLACK (she/they) has been heralded as “one of our premier gifted young science writers” and is the bestselling, award-winning author of several books, including When the Earth Was Green and The Last Days of the Dinosaurs. A science correspondent for Smithsonian and regular contributor to publications like National Geographic and Slate, Riley is a widely-recognized expert on paleontology. She won the 2024 Friend of Darwin Award from the National Center for Science Education.

 

About the Moderator: 

Tom Hall is WYPR's Senior News Analyst. He was the host of Midday, the award-winning, highly rated news and public policy program on WYPR Radio that featured interviews with elected officials, community leaders, as well as thought provoking authors, artists, researchers, journalists and scholars from around the world.

 

About the Program: 

To attend in person please register here.  Doors will open to registered attendees at 6 pm. A local bookseller will be on-site and have books available for purchase.Free parking vouchers are available to program attendees who park at the Franklin Street Garage (15 W. Franklin Street) after 4pm.  Ask Pratt event staff for your parking voucher prior to or after the program. This free event will be presented in-person and virtually.   This is a seated event with spaces reserved for individuals with accessibility needs. ASL interpretation will also be available for attendees throughout the event. name: (CS)²AI Online™ Symposium: Smart Building Cybersecurity
description:
### Panel A: When Hackers Cross into the Physical World — Ransomware and Building Systems

**Description:**
Attackers are no longer content with stealing data. In 2026 they have hacked refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores, causing spoiled food and fires. They have disrupted door access and HVAC at a hospital, and they have locked staff out of their own offices to force ransom payments. Building automation systems (BAS) control HVAC, access control, lighting, elevators and fire panels. Most of them run on protocols with no authentication, and they are rarely monitored. That makes them both leverage for extortion and a hidden way into corporate IT. This panel looks at how and why attackers target buildings, what a “physical consequence” attack looks like, and what owners, operators and integrators should do now.

### Presentation: Managing Smart Building Vendors: Practical Strategies to Reduce Cybersecurity and Operational Risk

***

### Panel B: Smarter Buildings, Smarter Attackers — AI, Regulation and Accountability

**Description:**
AI is entering building operations from both directions. Operators are deploying AI agents to optimize energy, comfort and maintenance. Attackers are using AI to learn obscure embedded systems and speed up reconnaissance. At the same time, regulation is catching up: NIS2 and the EU Cyber Resilience Act are bringing BAS into compliance scope. Insurers are demanding evidence of controls, and boards are being told that cyber risk to physical operations is a governance issue. This panel examines what AI changes in building cybersecurity, how emerging rules affect owners, manufacturers and integrators, and who should be accountable when a “smart” building is compromised.

### A Blockspace Community × Coffee&Code Collaboration

Before the hype. Before the buzzwords. Before “AI-powered everything.”

No panels. No pitches. No pressure.
Just good people, good coffee, and focused time to build, learn, and connect.

An open, welcoming space for coders, builders, designers, and curious minds.
Bring your own project, homework, startup, side quest, experiment, or idea. Work at your own pace, meet other builders, ask questions, exchange ideas, or simply enjoy being productive around like-minded people.
Expect:

* Focused building time
* Organic conversations
* Spontaneous debugging
* Knowledge sharing
* Genuine community

This meetup is beginner-friendly, expert-respected, and ego-free.

❌ A lecture
❌ A sales event
❌ A recruiting trap
❌ A 90-minute presentation

1. Show up

6. Leave having made progress—or at least a new friend

* Software engineers and data professionals

Whether this is your first Coffee&Code, you are part of the Blockspace Community, or you have been attending since day one, you are welcome.

threadHOURS

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: The Haunted House
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“The Haunted House,”** on scary dwellings and their grip on us, with Brittany Warman, former instructor at Ohio State University and co-founder of The Carterhaugh School of Folklore and the Fantastic.

[Doors open at 5. The talk starts at 6:30. The room is open seating. Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-the-haunted-house ](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-the-haunted-house )]

The haunted house has long held a place in the imaginations of those who enjoy a bit of uncanny terror, posing the ultimate threat to security and normalcy. It’s where something familiar becomes strange and unsettling, even threatening. You initially might have thought you're safe—after all, you should be safe indoors—but you're not. Sanctuary and shelter have turned against you. The very walls trouble your dreams.

Come tour some of the most terrifying real estate ever imagined with Brittany Warman, who has earned herself a large and devoted following among Profs and Pints audiences with excellent past talks on folklore, fairy tales, and horror.

She’ll show you the fascinating folkloric, literary, and real-world history of the haunted house. She’ll leave you wondering about the creepy old places in your town with doors that you’re afraid to approach on Halloween, and she might even leave you eager to turn your own home into such an eerie dwelling.

She’ll begin by discussing the scary structures of fairy tales, such as gingerbread houses and Bluebeard's castle, exploring how the early stories told about them influenced the terrifying tales of Henry James' Bly Manor and Edgar Allen Poe's House of Usher. She’ll consider the impact of haunted spaces on the Gothic and horror genres and explain why haunted houses are often so opulent and so decadent in their decay.

Among the questions Dr. Warman will tackle: What might the haunted house have to say about history, culture, and society? What draws us, again and again, to haunted houses, making us want to visit them, find their ghosts, and uncover their stories?

She'll conclude by examining how these tales still resonate today, in haunted houses both purportedly real and those decidedly fake, meant for shocks and thrills. Even Disney's Haunted Mansion ride will make an appearance. It’s a scary world after all. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID.)

Image: An abandoned house near Pocomoke City, Md., in 2008. (Photo by Matt Trostle / Creative Commons.)

name: Measuring Ledgers With The Blockchain Decentralisation Index Lab
description:
The new Blockchain Decentralisation Index Lab is an open source tool kit for measuring the decentralisation of distributed ledgers, layer by layer — consensus, tokenomics, network, software, and beyond.

The lab develops and maintains a suite of open source tools that collect data from live blockchain systems, parse it into a common format, and compute decentralisation metrics over it. Each tool targets a distinct layer of the stack and shares a common pipeline architecture (collect → parse → map to entities → apply metrics → publish).

Learn more about the Lab, how to use it and how to get involved in this online event. You can also find out more about the Lab at: [https://github.com/Blockchain-Decentralisation-Index](https://github.com/Blockchain-Decentralisation-Index)

You are also welcome to join the #bdi channel on the LFDT Discord at: [https://discord.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/](https://discord.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/)

name: Make your coding agents policy-aware: Platform guardrails for cloud and Kuberne…
description:
Coding agents write Terraform and Kubernetes manifests and spin up cloud services. They can’t see your guardrails, and they copy outdated patterns from the repo. Cost leaks, security gaps, and operational misses slip through. Reviews drag. Tickets pile up. Learn how to make agents aware of the policies you already run, and how runtime enforcement catches the rest.

In this webinar, we will explore:
1. Why agent-written infrastructure breaks the detect-and-ticket model, and what it costs platform, FinOps, and security teams in reviews, blocked deploys, and rework.
2. How to give coding agents real-time awareness of the cost, security, and operational policies you already run, so Terraform and Kubernetes changes are compliant before they ship.
3. Why runtime enforcement and automated remediation still matter for drift, manual changes, and live workloads across cloud and Kubernetes.

name: Youth RPG Club — Kids on Bikes

You know that feeling in Stranger Things when the kids are the only ones who understand what is really happening? When the adults are too busy, too skeptical, too caught up in the ordinary world to see the darkness gathering at the edges of it? That is Kids on Bikes.


In this tabletop roleplaying game, you and your friends play ordinary kids in an ordinary neighborhood. You ride your bikes. You know your streets. And you are the only ones who know what is coming.


Because something is coming.


The adults cannot see it. Maybe they will not. Maybe they cannot. That part does not matter.

What matters is that your neighborhood needs defending, your friends need you, and the only weapons you have are your courage, your wits, and each other.


No controllers. No screens. Just a table, some friends, some dice, and a story that belongs to everyone in the room.


Inspired by the storytelling of Stranger Things, E.T., and Stand By Me. No experience necessary. Sign up for all sessions, if possible. If not, reach out to info@churchonthesquarebaltimore.org to be prepared for a drop in session.

name: Emily Rosenthal: "Leroy Has Something to Say"
description:
Leroy the ghost loves his garden at Rosebud Manor. Every time a new family moves in, he greets them with a beautiful yellow rose, the flower of friendship. But no one understands what he's trying to say, and they always get scared away!

 

Then one day, Tara-a girl who uses a device to talk-moves in. It turns out Tara knows just as much about plants as Leroy. Is it possible she speaks the language of flowers, too, and that Leroy has finally found someone who understands him?

 

This sweet picture book celebrates the many different ways we communicate with each other, showing there's more than one way to find your voice and make a friend.

 

About the Author:

Emily Rosenthal (she/her) is a writer and illustrator based in Baltimore, Maryland. She loves ghosts, monsters, and all kinds of creatures, and frequently tells stories about them. When not coming up with stories, Emily plays soccer, watches scary movies, and snuggles with her cat. She’s thankful for everyone who has believed she has something important to say. Leroy Has Something to Say is her first picture book.

name: Maryland Higher Education Environmental Literacy Summit 2026
description:
Empowering educators, cultivating stewards: Bridging campus and community through environmental education”
The Higher Education Environmental Literacy (HEEL) Summit is a statewide gathering where college and university faculty, specializing in teacher education, converge with non-formal environmental education providers. The summit aims to foster collaboration and innovation to enhance environmental and climate literacy within Maryland teacher preparation programs.
Together, we’ll explore new strategies, share best practices, and forge partnerships to ensure future educators are equipped to inspire the next generation of environmental stewards.
Lunch & parking will be provided.

name: Outfall Screening Blitz - Stony Run
description:
Learn about water quality testing with the scientists of Blue Water Baltimore! An Outfall Screening Blitz consists of taking teams of volunteers into our local streams to sample water quality. The events take place 48 hours after a major rain event to ensure stormwater is not being sampled. Samples will be collected from streams being monitored where dry weather flow is coming from a stormwater outfall. We will discuss different types of pollution, how it is entering our waterways and steps you can take to help report and prevent pollution from happening. PLEASE NOTE: This is a limited capacity event.

name: “Fled to the Spirit World”: The Victorian Spiritualists of Green Mount Cemetery
description:
Join staff from the library's Maryland Department on Friday, October 30th at Green Mount Cemetery for the 6th program in our series on the Dark Side of Maryland!

 

Discover Green Mount Cemetery’s long hidden and mysterious history. During the tour, we will visit the gravesite of Elijah Bond, who patented the Ouija Board, as well as the final resting places of prominent Spiritualists of nineteenth-century Baltimore. Librarian Julie Saylor will tell their stories, gleaned from family histories, newspaper accounts, and their own writings.

 

Meet at the main gate, 1501 Greenmount Avenue. The tour will be rain or shine. Participants should come prepared to walk on stone paths and uneven ground.

This is program 6 in our 6 part Dark Side of Maryland series. If you are interested in attending any other programs to hear about Maryland's darker side, check these out:

October 6 -- Unveiling Maryland's MonstersOctober 13 -- Maryland MayhemOctober 14 -- Witch's BrewOctober 20 -- Mediums, Magicians and the Ouija BoardOctober 27 -- Haunted MarylandOctober 30 & 31 -- Green Mount spiritualism cemetery tour 

Registration for this event is required.  Register here.

description:
### [Modern SOC Skills: Cisco XDR + Splunk for Faster Threat Detection & Response](https://cutt.ly/lyQBhBGt)

Cybersecurity threats are becoming more complex, while IT and security teams are working with growing volumes of alerts, security data, and connected systems.
To mark **Cybersecurity Awareness Month**, NetCom Learning is hosting this **complimentary 1-hour webinar** on how modern security operations teams can improve threat detection, investigation, prioritization, and response using **Cisco XDR and Splunk**.
Register now
The session will explore how security teams can bring together relevant context, reduce investigation effort, and use connected workflows and automation to support faster security decisions.

###

### What We’ll Cover

* Modern SOC challenges and alert overload
* Security data, risk, and incident context
* Threat investigation with Cisco XDR
* Security analytics with Splunk
* Connected XDR + Splunk workflows
* SOC automation and modern security skills

### Who Should Join?

Ideal for **IT and cybersecurity professionals, security teams, engineers, administrators, technical leaders, and anyone interested in modern SOC operations**.
No advanced Cisco XDR or Splunk experience is required.

###

### Event Details

**Date:** Friday, October 30, 2026
**Time:** 12 PM ET
**Format:** Online Webinar
**Duration:** 1 Hour
**Cost:** **Complimentary / Free to Attend**
Join us this Cybersecurity Awareness Month to strengthen your understanding of modern threat detection, investigation, and response.

name: NEC Drop-in: BOOtiful Bats
description:
October’s theme, Nocturnal Animals of Cylburn, focuses on animals that become active as the sun goes down. Each Saturday will highlight a different nocturnal animal that calls Cylburn Arboretum home and explore the adaptations that help them thrive at night. While some creatures of the night sometimes get a spooky reputation, we’ll shed some light on these often misunderstood animals and discover there’s much more to admire than fear!

Please note: NO live animals will be present during these programs.

All ages are welcome. No fee or registration required (supplies limited). Drop-in anytime between 11am to 12pm.

October 3: Observant Owls

Whooo’s awake when the sun goes down? Drop by the Nature Education Center to discover the owls that call Cylburn home and uncover the adaptations that make these nighttime hunters so well suited for life after dark. 

October 10: Remarkable Raccoons

There’s a ‘masked’ visitor roaming Cylburn after dark! A raccoon’s distinctive black mask provides camouflage and helps reduce glare. Drop by the Nature Education Center to find out more about the adaptations that help them thrive at night.

October 17: Fantastic Flying squirrels

Something is soaring through the trees but it isn’t a bird or a bat! Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn more about how these small nocturnal mammals glide through the forest after dark. 

October 24: Outstanding Opossums

What’s lurking around Cylburn after dark? It might be an opossum!  Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn more about the only marsupials in North America and how they help the environment.

October 31: BOOtiful Bats

This Halloween, discover the bats that fly over Cylburn after sunset. Drop by the Nature Education Center to learn how these nocturnal mammals navigate the darkness and play an important role in our ecosystem.

name: One Maryland One Book Discussion: No Sense in Wishing
description:
Join the Pratt Page-Turners Book Club for a discussion of the 2026 One Maryland One Book selection, No Sense in Wishing: Essays on Black Music, Belonging, and Baltimore by Lawrence Burney.

 

No Sense in Wishing: Essays on Black Music, Belonging, and Baltimore by Lawrence Burney is a personal and analytical essay collection that showcases his home city of Baltimore, music from throughout the global Black diaspora, and the traditions that raised him. Each essay draws on formative moments and cultural artifacts to tell the story of our region’s cultural scene through Burney's unique point of view. Written by one of our contemporary rising cultural critics, the book aptly captures this year’s One Maryland One Book theme of Revolution, Reaction, and Reform.


This program has a hybrid format. Participate either in person or on Zoom.
 


For help obtaining a copy of the book or more information about the book club, please email fic@prattlibrary.org.

 

Free parking validation stickers will be available to program attendees who park at the Franklin Street Garage (15 W. Franklin Street) while supplies last. Take a ticket when you enter the garage, and ask Pratt event staff for your parking validation sticker prior to or after the program.

name: W29 CSTGIA 2026: From Strategic Cyber Foresight to Adaptive Cyber Enterprises
description:
### From Adaptive Cyber Enterprises to Anticipatory Cyber Leadership: Shaping the Future Before Others Recognize It

What separates organizations that merely adapt from those that shape the future?

In this episode of Creating Something That Gives It All Away (CSTGIA), we explore the next evolution of executive leadership: Anticipatory Cyber Leadership. As artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, cybersecurity threats, and digital transformation accelerate, organizations can no longer afford to simply react to disruption, they must learn to anticipate emerging trends, engineer opportunity, and prepare for futures that have not yet arrived.

Together, we'll examine the five leadership shifts that distinguish tomorrow's leaders from today's managers, including moving from adaptation to anticipation, risk management to opportunity engineering, AI assistance to executive decision intelligence, strategic planning to continuous future design, and organizational learning to ecosystem leadership. Discover how leaders can strengthen strategic curiosity, systems thinking, decision intelligence, human-AI collaboration, and learning velocity to build organizations that don't just survive change, they create it.

In this episode you'll learn:
(1) Why leadership, not technology, is becoming the greatest competitive advantage
(2) The five leadership shifts driving anticipatory organizations
(3) How AI can strengthen executive decision-making without replacing human judgment
(4) Practical strategies for preparing your organization before disruption occurs
(5) How to develop the mindset and capabilities needed to shape the future instead of reacting to it

If you enjoy this content, please Like, Subscribe, and Share to help others prepare for the future of cybersecurity, leadership, and digital transformation.

name: Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses
description:
## Claude Code vs. Codex: Loops, Graphs, and Harnesses

This is a casual pair-programming meetup for developers experimenting with Claude Code, Codex, and agentic coding workflows.
There is no formal presentation and no fixed curriculum. Bring a laptop, a repository, a side project, or a workflow you want to test. We will work in small groups, compare approaches, debug problems, and share what is working.

Possible areas to explore include:

* Building iterative coding-agent loops
* Comparing Claude Code and Codex on the same task
* Designing graph-based agent workflows
* Creating reusable coding harnesses
* Managing context across large repositories
* Running tests and validating agent-generated changes
* Using sandboxes, permissions, and approval steps
* Coordinating subagents or parallel tasks
* Measuring latency, token usage, cost, and completion quality
* Debugging failed or incomplete agent runs

You do not need to be an expert in either tool. This meetup is for people who want hands-on time to experiment, pair with other developers, and learn through building.
Bring something you are working on, or join someone else’s project.
Hosted by **CODE**.

description:

In this class, we teach kids how to meditate plus introduce them to foundational Buddhist concepts such as: how to connect to a sense of inner peace, to identify with our astounding potential, develop compassion and gratitude for the kindness of others, and let go of agitating states of mind like anger and jealousy.

Regular attendance at these classes can assist kids with the development of important life skills such as increased empathy, respect for others, self control and concentration.

name: Visit to BMA: Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography
description:
Visit to BMA: Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography

For our weekly Platform for November 1 at 11 AM, we will visit the Baltimore Museum of Art, located at 10 Art Museum Dr, Baltimore, MD 21218.

We will visit the photographic exhibition entitle, "Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography." David Lavine, a BES member and photographer, will join us to share his experience with us.

We have purchased a limited number of tickets to be given free to BES Members. If you're not a member and wish to join us on 11/1 at 11 AM, you can purchase your tickets on line. Please reserve your tickets early.

We will meet in the East Entrance by Gertrude's at BMA, 11 AM. Afterwards, we may gather for lunch.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

https://artbma.org/exhibition/flashback-baltimore-photography/

Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography
Date: October 4, 2026 - February 21, 2027
Price: BMA Members: Free \| Adults: $15 \| Seniors\, Active\-duty U\.S\. Military & BMA Member Guests: $13 \| Groups: $12/person \| Students & Youth: $5 \| Children 6 & Under: Free \| Discounted admission Thursdays after 5 p\.m\.

Reserve Tickets:
https://reservations.artbma.org/orders/601/calendar?eventId=6a8da4bf67b18ab5366f2c43&cart&_gl=1\*1plkgn7\*_ga\*MTI3MTM4OTE5Mi4xNzkyNTQzMjAz\*_ga_Z89PXM15R3\*czE3OTI2MDcxNDYkbzIkZzAkdDE3OTI2MDcxNDYkajYwJGwwJGgw

Experience the first major exhibition to examine Baltimore's pivotal role in the history of photography.

Featuring more than 200 images spanning 185 years, Flashback traces photography in Baltimore from its earliest forms to unforgettable contemporary works. From rare daguerreotypes and Civil War–era photographs to images captured during landmark cultural moments of our time, the exhibition shows photography evolving across generations and offers a rich, nuanced portrait of Baltimore.

New research and fresh perspectives bring to light photographers whose work has often been obscured by gender and racial prejudices. The exhibition shows how photography not only records history but also shapes it, by asking: Who gets to take pictures? Who is seen? And how are images shared?

Exhibition Highlights:
Images by Arthur Laidler Macbeth, founder of one of the city’s earliest Black-owned portrait studios, and
Dora Russell, who established one of Baltimore’s first woman-owned portrait studios, that show how access
to a camera allowed for new forms of visibility.
Rare daguerreotypes, tintypes, and Civil War–era photographs that reveal how photography quickly became entangled with questions of labor, race, mobility, and power.
Poignant examples of photojournalism from Irving Henry Phillips Sr.’s decades of work at the Afro-American newspaper, where he recorded Black life in Baltimore as a subject of national importance.
Selections from landmark documentary projects of the 1970s, a period that saw multiple surveys dedicated to recording Baltimore’s neighborhoods and the ethnic communities within them.
Gripping images from the 2015 Baltimore Uprising and 2020 Black Lives Matter protests taken by Devin Allen, Sheila Pree Bright, Joseph Mario Giordano, and Shawn Hubbard that record the urgency of those moments and frame them as a collective experience rather than a distant event.

description:
Zoom link: [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)

Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth

Talk #1: Homa: A Fast Lane for Small Messages
by John Ousterhout, Professor Emeritus of Computer Science at Stanford University

John will explain how Homa can dramatically reduce small-message latency and explore its potential relevance to AI workloads. Drawing on his expertise in transport protocols, he’ll discuss what Homa could offer when small-message latency matters. Its importance for AI workloads remains an open, workload-dependent question.

description:
How did enslaved Africans turn America’s infamous failure into the greatest moral occasion of modern Western life? In this book, Christopher Freeburg answers that question with one word: soul. It was soul, Freeburg believes, which drove Black individuals and communities, grappling with horrific strife, to reimagine American life and equality in earnest.

 

Black cultural life contains a central and significant theme—a soul, or form of life—expressed in a variety of musical, religious, and political forms. Through the work and words of figures ranging from the poet Phillis Wheatley to President Barack Obama and musician Nina Simone to disco owner Jewel Thais-Williams, Freeburg shows how Black communities leaned time and again on soul and its four pillars: resonance, revelation, resilience, and transcendence. It is soul, what Freeburg calls a beautiful transaction between individual and community across time and place, that has allowed Black people over generations to transform feelings of defeat and alienation into moral courage and shared belonging.

 

Christopher Freeburg will be joined in conversation by The Atlantic's senior editor Vann Newkirk. 

 

About the Author: 

Christopher Freeburg is the Presidential Humanities and Social Sciences Chair in English at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign. His most recent book was Counterlife: Slavery after Resistance and Social Death.

 

About the Moderator: 

Vann Newkirk is a senior editor at The Atlantic and the host of the podcasts Floodlines and Holy Week.

 

About the Program: 

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 6 pm. A local bookseller will be on-site and have books available for purchase.Free parking vouchers are available to program attendees who park at the Franklin Street Garage (15 W. Franklin Street) after 4pm.  Ask Pratt event staff for your parking voucher prior to or after the program. This free event will be presented in-person and virtually.   This is a seated event with spaces reserved for individuals with accessibility needs. ASL interpretation will also be available for attendees throughout the event. If you need additional accommodations to successfully participate, please let us know at events@prattlibrary.org or 443-768-0762.

In recent months, AI has fundamentally reshaped cybersecurity. Automated tooling now discovers open-source vulnerabilities and generates exploits at unprecedented speeds. As the sheer volume and velocity of CVE disclosures overwhelm traditional workflows, IT and security teams face a daunting challenge: How do you patch rapidly without destabilizing mission-critical production environments?
Join us for the next [Philadelphia Red Hat User Group (RHUG)](https://reg.experiences.redhat.com/flow/redhat/4900050/rhexpressregistration/page/expressregistration?sc_cid=RHCTN1260000495451) to explore how Red Hat turns the tide on AI-driven threats by securing the software supply chain from code to deployment.
What we'll cover:

* Red Hat Trusted Libraries: How cryptographically signed, SLSA-compliant binaries neutralize upstream risks before code hits production.
* Project Lightwell: How automated, validated patching and backports maintain enterprise stability in an AI-accelerated threat landscape.
* Peer Networking: Connect with local IT leaders and Red Hat experts over food and drinks at Philly's newest high-energy venue.

name: WP Site Management Tools
description:
A common question that comes up repeatedly is "what is the best tool to manage websites for ME". Cause different people have different needs.

We've invited the 3 main players in the "done for you" WP management and we'll interview them about their features so that you can compare them in a more "apples to apples" way and make your own decision about what's best for you.

The tools:
\- ManageWP\, WP Remote\, and WP Umbrella are confirmed\.

The topics:

\- Backups & restoration
\- Manual & automated updates
\- Plugin/theme management across sites
\- User management \(both on the tool & on WP sites\)
\- Security/vulnerability
\- Reports
\- Broken links/Performance/Uptime/Site health monitoring
\- AI
\- GDPR & privacy compliance
\- Any other special features

The format:

10 topics, each tool gets 2 min to talk about what they do for the topic. So people can listen to topics that matter most to them and get the three tools one after the other.

I'll introduce the topic, ie: Backups & restoration with a 15-30 second intro then each product owner gets 2 minutes to talk about their product and their product ONLY.

You'll be muted on entry, we'll be using the chat to queue people up/ask follow-on questions.

The meetup is scheduled for 11am ET until 12:30pm ET.

Meetup is scheduled to be recorded. Recordings are posted about 2 weeks after the meetup and are provided courtesy of our sponsor, [Obee Digital Consulting](https://obeedigitalconsulting.com/).

How to get notified about the recording: either subscribe to the [youtube channel](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLoT0wv53Bj-BGfD8fPhMRC3qTtPMZHioI), RSVP "yes" to the meetup, or [join the mailing list](https://share.mailercloud.com/form?id=a0NzdUAxMTI1OUAwMDAwMA==).

name: 3 platform requirements for agentic engineering
description:
Agentic engineering only works if the platform underneath it can support autonomous action safely. Justin Billig and Dan Rye, co-founders of Tensure, break down the three platform capabilities engineering organizations need to move agents out of experimentation and into production: a controlled action layer, identity and guardrails, and a feedback loop.

**You'll come away knowing:**

1. How to build a controlled action layer that exposes approved capabilities to agents through APIs, Infrastructure as Code, and GitOps rather than direct infrastructure access.
2. How to give each agent an identity, scoped permissions, and explicit boundaries so autonomy stays bounded and humans approve what matters.
3. How to close the feedback loop with observability, testing, policy checks, SLOs, and audit data so agents know whether an action worked and can respond when it didn't.

name: When Building Gets Cheap, Judgment Gets Expensive
description:
AI is dramatically reducing the cost and time required to build software. That doesn’t make product strategy less important. It makes bad judgment easier to execute at scale.

This talk examines what changes when teams can build almost anything: how to choose better bets, make real tradeoffs, distinguish faster execution from faster learning, and keep speed from turning into more chaos. Drawing from *[The Strategy Cycle](https://thestrategycycle.com/)*, [Andrew Skotzko](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andrewskotzko) will share a practical way to decide what to build, what not to build, and what has to be true for a bet to work.

Mind the Product founder Martin Eriksson says the book shows you what to do on Monday morning—and “what to do in week 7 when the strategy is quietly falling apart.”

Marty Cagan, Founder of the Silicon Valley Product Group, adds, "Andrew is a proven product leader and product leadership coach who has set out to help product leaders with one of the most important yet most difficult responsibilities of product leadership: creating a winning product strategy."

AGENDA
6:00 - 6:15 pm: Welcome and Registration. Snacks and refreshments provided.
6:15 - 7:30 pm: Talk and Q&A
7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking

description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

Timothy Tyson and Mary Williams: "Mahalia Jackson, Moving on Up a Little Higher"
description:
If Americans today still recognize the name Mahalia Jackson, they might recall that she was perhaps the greatest gospel singer who ever lived. But for many people, there is no awareness at all, not even for an entertainer whose “Move On Up a Little Higher” sold eight million copies, who headlined two Newport Jazz Festivals and performed before four United States presidents.

 

While this rich musical legacy is admired by those in the know, virtually no one recognizes Jackson’s astonishing role in American civil rights history. In this startling new depiction of the renowned gospel singer, New York Times best-selling author Timothy B. Tyson and Mary D. Williams, an acclaimed gospel singer herself, bring Jackson back to soaring life by positioning her as the major civil rights figure she, in fact, was.

 

Mahlia Jackson, Moving On Up a Little Higher then traces Jackson’s career from abject poverty in New Orleans to global superstardom, revealing how even after meteoric success, Jackson maintained an unwavering devotion to Black freedom. In the 1930s in Chicago, even before the Civil Rights Movement took its modern shape, she used her rapturous voice to support independent Black political power. Her work only intensified in the 1940s and beyond when she campaigned first for Franklin D. Roosevelt, and later for Harry Truman, John F. Kennedy, and Lyndon B. Johnson; headlined in Montgomery for the 1955–56 bus boycott; sang for the Birmingham campaign and on the Selma March; and performed at the iconic 1963 March on Washington, where she urged Martin Luther King Jr. to “Tell ’em about the dream.” In retrospect what becomes historically significant is that Mahalia Jackson was present at so many civil rights events, even singing a divine rendition of “Precious Lord, Take My Hand,” at Dr. King’s funeral in 1968. Weakened and worn, she succumbed to heart failure four years later at the age of sixty.

 

Weaving together Mahalia Jackson’s inspiring life journey with her soulful music into a transcendent text, this biography ultimately casts Mahalia Jackson as we’ve never seen her before, as a guiding light for the Civil Rights Movement, whose message still speaks to our struggles today.

 

Timothy B. Tyson and Mary D. Williams will be joined in conversation by The Atlantic's senior editor Vann Newkirk. 

 

About the Authors: 

Timothy B. Tyson is senior research scholar at the Center for Documentary Studies at Duke University and the author of five books, including New York Times bestseller The Blood of Emmett Till.

 

Mary D. Williams is a gospel singer, civil rights historian, and former adjunct professor at Duke University. She has performed at the Kennedy Center and the Metropolitan Museum of Art and lives in Garner, North Carolina.

 

About the Moderator: 

Vann Newkirk is a senior editor at The Atlantic and the host of the podcasts Floodlines and Holy Week.

 

About the Program: 

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 6 pm. A local bookseller will be on-site and have books available for purchase.Free parking vouchers are available to program attendees who park at the Franklin Street Garage (15 W. Franklin Street) after 4pm.  Ask Pratt event staff for your parking voucher prior to or after the program. This free event will be presented in-person and virtually.   This is a seated event with spaces reserved for individuals with accessibility needs. ASL interpretation will also be available for attendees throughout the event. If you need additional accommodations to successfully participate, please let us know at events@prattlibrary.org or 443-768-0762.

RSVPing only on the Meetup Page doesn't allow you to attend the Event. ADVANCE TICKET PURCHASE IS REQUIRED.

ABOUT THE EVENT

You are cordially invited to join us at the Embassy of Zimbabwe for a night filled with fun and information on the country's culture, economy, business and mainly tourism.
Witness the majesty of wildlife roaming free in the National Parks, feel the spray of the mighty Victoria Falls and experience the warmth of Zimbabweans whose hospitality shines with genuine joy, and no visit is complete without indulging in Zimbabwe’s rich **gastronomy**.

Zimbabwe has several major tourist attractions. Victoria Falls on the Zambezi river is one of them. It is considered to be the largest waterfall in the world.
The Victoria Falls National Park is also in this area and is one of the eight main national parks in the country. The largest of which is Hwange National Park. Lake Kariba another site for tourism, is the largest reservoir in the world.

Zimbabwe is unusual in Africa in that there are a number of ancient and medieval ruined cities built in a unique dry stone style. Among the most famous of these are the Great Zimbabwe ruins in Masvingo.

Zimbabwe is also the third largest producer of platinum and one of the largest producers of gold.

For Google Chrome Users :
1\. Open Google Chrome\.

5\. Select Block Pop\-ups and turn it off\.

name: Pop-Up Display: Lichens
description:
What’s to like about Lichens? 

You might see crusty, scaly patches on your trees, benches, rocks, or even a garbage can and think they are a problem. But lichens are a true partnership of two different organisms (fungi and algae) that serve as a food source and habitat for many animals and provide valuable environmental and health benefits to humans by acting as natural air monitors, helping form soil, and offering medicinal properties. 

Join Master Naturalist Pat Jonas in the Nature Education Center to discover how to identify the different kinds of lichens, where you might find them and learn more about what makes these organisms so important to our ecosystem.

name: W30 CSTGIA 2026: Cognitive Cyber Enterprises
description:
### From Anticipatory Cyber Leadership to Cognitive Cyber Enterprises

Artificial intelligence is becoming ubiquitous. Autonomous systems are proliferating. Data is abundant. Yet many organizations still struggle with fragmented decisions, disconnected knowledge, and organizational silos.

In this week's Cyber & STEAM Global Innovation Alliance (CSTGIA) Spotlight on What's Next 2026 – Week 30, Dr. Rhonda Farrell explores the next evolution of cybersecurity leadership: the transition from Anticipatory Cyber Leadership to Cognitive Cyber Enterprises.

Discover how leading organizations are transforming cybersecurity from a technical function into an enterprise-wide intelligence capability by connecting people, policy, process, platforms, governance, AI, and knowledge into a unified decision ecosystem.

In this session you'll learn:
• Why enterprise intelligence is becoming the next competitive advantage
• The five strategic moves toward Cognitive Cyber Enterprises
• How connected decisions outperform connected databases
• Why AI must orchestrate knowledge—not simply automate tasks
• How collective intelligence strengthens resilience, governance, and innovation
• Practical leadership questions to help your organization continuously learn, adapt, and improve

The organizations that lead tomorrow won't simply deploy smarter technology, they'll build enterprises that become smarter every single day.

Because the future belongs to organizations that continuously improve how they think, not just what they do.

🎥 **Watch on YouTube:** https://youtu.be/x0vEk5buU98

If you enjoy this content, please Like, Subscribe, and Share to help others prepare for the future of cybersecurity, leadership, and digital transformation.

🔔 New episodes of CSTGIA 2026 are released weekly, exploring the emerging trends, technologies, leadership strategies, and enterprise capabilities shaping the future of cybersecurity and organizational excellence.

#Cybersecurity #ArtificialIntelligence #EnterpriseArchitecture #DigitalTransformation #CyberLeadership #KnowledgeManagement #AIGovernance #Innovation #Leadership #FutureOfWork #DecisionIntelligence #CSTGIA

description:
## Claude Code Saturdays 🤖💻

**A weekly hands-on meetup for builders using Claude to write, refactor, and reason about code.**
Claude Code Saturdays is a relaxed, collaborative session for developers, founders, and tinkerers who want to explore what’s possible with Anthropic’s Claude for real-world coding tasks. * 🧠 **Reasoning-heavy tasks**: debugging, architecture, tests, and docs

* ☕ **Casual, friendly atmosphere**—bring your laptop and curiosity

### Who Should Attend

* Software engineers (any level)
* Startup founders and indie hackers
* Students learning to code with AI
* Anyone curious about AI-assisted development with Claude

You don’t need to be an expert—just a willingness to experiment and learn together.

* A laptop

Let’s spend our Saturdays building smarter, faster, and more thoughtfully—with Claude as our coding companion.

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: How Ancient Athens Restored Democracy
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“How Ancient Athens Restored Democracy,”** on lessons to be learned from an overthrow of tyrants in 403 B.C., with Nicholas D. Cross, assistant professor of history at the United States Naval Academy and author of *The Roots of Cooperation: Constructing Interstate Alliances in Ancient Greece.*

[Doors open at 3. The talk starts at 4:30. The room is open seating. Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-athens-democracy](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-athens-democracy) ]

The defeat of Athens in the Peloponnesian War led to its democracy being replaced by the Thirty Tyrants, an oligarchic regime that consolidated power through executions and political repression. Democratic exiles managed to organize resistance, defeat the oligarchic forces, and return to Athens to restore democratic government, but then faced the far more challenging task of reconciling a community torn apart by political divisions.

The restorers of Athenian democracy grappled with a question that often arises in periods of political upheaval: Can a deeply divided community ever overcome its past and build a shared future? Learn how they managed to bring about such an outcome in a talk that holds hopeful lessons for our own time.

The speaker, Dr. Nicholas Cross, teaches the history of ancient Greece and Rome and is the author of a forthcoming biography of the leader of democratic resistance to the *Thirty Tyrants, Thrasybulus of Steiria: An Athenian Hero?*

He’ll describe how the settlement that followed the civil war included an amnesty designed to prevent cycles of retaliation, but Athens nonetheless remained deeply divided. Among those who had to find a way to live together once more were former democrats, supporters of oligarchy, and citizens such as Socrates whose conduct during the regime was open to question.

Democracy’s return was not a straightforward triumph. It instead involved dealing with tensions and making political decisions intended to enable peaceful coexistence possible. The Athenians had to balance both accountability with reconciliation and the desire for revenge with the need for lasting political stability.

The events of 403 BC remind us that rebuilding a divided society requires not only restoring political institutions but also reviving trust and learning to coexist with former adversaries. The lessons they learned in the process remain relevant nearly 2500 years later. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID.)

Image: The Acropolis at Athens as painted by Leo von Klenze in 1846 (Neue Pinakothek museum / Wikimedia Commons).

name: Applied AI Ethics MonthlyMixer - Where Innovation Meets Responsibility
description:
Join a global, open-format gathering for those building and questioning AI — from real-world use cases to critical conversations around ethics, bias, and transparency.
Every month, we create space for developers, researchers, and policymakers to connect in meaningful, unmoderated dialogue — with flexible chats, peer learning, and 1-on-1 video networking.
Watch how it works: **[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bOYkxBjrAYY](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bOYkxBjrAYY)**
**What Is the Applied AI & Ethics #MonthlyMixer?**
The Applied AI & Ethics MonthlyMixer is a self-directed online networking event where professionals from across the AI spectrum come together to collaborate, question, and connect.
This isn’t a webinar or panel — it’s a structured-free, chat-first environment hosted on a Slack-like virtual platform, featuring topic-specific channels and private video or text chat options.
Whether you're designing algorithms, drafting policy, or advocating for responsible tech, this is your space to exchange ideas, showcase projects, or meet others who care about building AI with integrity and impact.
**Who Should Join:**

* AI/ML developers working on real-world deployments
* Policy makers and legal experts exploring AI governance
* Data scientists interested in ethical model design
* Academics and researchers studying AI and society
* Ethicists, community leaders, and social impact advocates
* Product leaders balancing innovation with responsibility

Whether you're launching applied AI tools or questioning their societal effects, this mixer welcomes your perspective.
**Explore These Channels Inside:**
The platform provides themed group discussions to help you navigate the topics that matter most:

* #general – Start with introductions, announcements, and cross-topic conversation
* #networking – Share your portfolio, white papers, startups, or ethical AI tools
* #intros – Tell your story: what you work on and why it matters
* #help-wanted – Request or offer guidance around data ethics, fairness, or responsible deployment
* #industry-room-tech – Dive deep into real-world cases, AI misuse, explainability, and bias mitigation

You’ll also be able to chat directly and launch 1-on-1 video calls for deeper conversations.
**When & Where?**

* Second Wednesday of Every month
* 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM (your local time)
* Register from the platform here - [https://events.tao.ai/pod/analytics.club/cont-r8tfbvicrqsh](https://events.tao.ai/pod/analytics.club/cont-r8tfbvicrqsh)

No login hurdles. No presentations. Just people-driven dialogue.
**Why Join?**

* Global gathering of AI professionals shaping the future responsibly
* Self-led chats & 1-on-1 networking with values-aligned peers
* Exchange insights, frameworks, and use cases for applied AI
* Build your ethical AI toolkit and collaborative network
* Reconnect monthly to deepen the conversation

**Questions or Suggestions?**
We’re always listening.
Contact us anytime at: [https://noworkerleftbehind.org/event_support](https://noworkerleftbehind.org/event_support)

name: Profs & Pints Baltimore: How Acupuncture Became American
description:
[Profs and Pints Baltimore](https://www.profsandpints.com/baltimore) presents: **“How Acupuncture Became American,”** on an alternative form of medicine’s journey from the margins to the mainstream of our medical system, with Tom Ingegno, former graduate level instructor of East Asian Medicine, former Chair of the Maryland State Board of Acupuncture, and lecturer to universities, healthcare organizations, and government agencies.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-acupuncture](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/baltimore-acupuncture) .]

Acupuncture, once regarded in the United States as mysterious and foreign, now is well-known here as a licensed health profession. How did an unfamiliar Asian medical practice become mainstream health care and recognizable enough to turn up in comedy sketches, animated films, and pop culture? What changed as Americans translated the Asian practice of acupuncture for use here?

Learn the strange, surprising story of acupuncture in the United States with Tom Ingegno, 25-year practitioner of East Asian medicine, founder of Charm City Integrative Health, and author of *The Cupping Book: Unlocking the Secrets of Ancient Healing.*

You’ll learn how acupuncture’s journey into American medicine was anything but straightforward. In fact, it ended up taking three very different routes to become widely accepted here.

The first was diplomacy and journalism, with its way being paved by New York Times reporter James Reston’s 1971 account of receiving acupuncture after surgery in China, as well as the enormous attention surrounding Richard Nixon’s trip to China in 1972.

The second was activism, including acupuncture-based addiction treatment developed at Lincoln Hospital in the South Bronx by people associated with the Young Lords, Black Panthers, and the community health movement.

The third was via mass culture and professionalization. Americans learned about acupuncture through magazine coverage, television, movies, music, and celebrity use. The nation witnessed the rise of a distinctly American acupuncture profession through the gradual creation of schools, licensing systems, and professional organizations.

The talk will end with a quick visual tour of acupuncture in American popular culture. Audience members will be left with a much richer understanding of how health practices come to be accepted. (Doors: $17, or $15 with a student ID. Bar doors open at 5 pm. The talk starts at 6:30.)

Image: Acupuncture being administered by a U.S. Navy specialist to a service member (Marine Corps photo).

name: Building Privacy Preserving Token Applications Using Panurus
description:
Panurus ([https://github.com/LFDT-Panurus](https://github.com/LFDT-Panurus)) is an open-source framework for building token-based applications that preserve transactional privacy while remaining fully auditable and interoperable across ledgers. In this talk, we'll walk through how Panurus's driver-based architecture lets developers plug in different token technologies — from Fabtoken to zero-knowledge schemes — behind a common transaction lifecycle (Request → Assemble → Sign → Commit), and how this enables privacy-preserving applications without locking you into a single blockchain or cryptographic scheme.

We'll also spotlight two mentorship programs currently pushing Panurus's capabilities forward:

**\- EVM Network Driver** — extending Panurus with support for EVM-compatible chains, bringing privacy-preserving tokens to Ethereum and its ecosystem.
**\- zkat\-snark Driver** — introducing a zk-SNARK-based anonymous token driver, expanding Panurus's toolkit for confidential, provably-correct transactions.

Come see how these efforts are shaping Panurus's roadmap, and how you can get involved.

**Zoom Meeting Link**: [https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09](https://zoom.us/my/hyperledger.community.3?pwd=UE90WHhEaHRqOGEyMkV3cldKa2d2dz09)

name: Near-zero time to resolution: Agentic workflows for failed and drifted IaC
description:
When infrastructure fails or drifts, resolution still looks like it did a decade ago: a human reads logs, pieces together what changed and hand-writes a fix. Artem Artyunov of env zero demos a different path: an AI coding assistant and a custom skill from Git, asking a live IaC platform which environments failed, what drifted and what the safe fix is.

We'll cover:
1\. Asking plain-language questions of a live infrastructure-as-code platform through its CLI, using an AI coding assistant and a custom skill loaded from Git.
2\. See how the skill is built, and how authentication and guardrails keep the agent from doing anything you didn't approve.
3\. A working pattern you can adapt to your own IaC tooling, and a realistic view of what agentic remediation can and can't do today, including where human review still belongs.

A proposed response action plan (RAP) has been submitted to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) for approval. Site investigations found petroleum-impacted soil, petroleum- and hexavalent chromium-impacted groundwater, and volatile organic compound-impacted soil vapor in limited areas of the site. name: W31 CSTGIA 2026: Cognitive Cyber Enterprises
description:
### When AI Can Act Independently\, Trust Must Become an Enterprise System \| CSTGIA Week 31

What happens when AI stops simply recommending what humans should do—and begins acting on our behalf?

Welcome to CSTGIA 2026 Week 31: From Cognitive Cyber Enterprises to Autonomous Trust Ecosystems.

Agentic AI is rapidly changing the cybersecurity and governance equation. Intelligent agents can execute multi-step workflows, interact with other systems, access organizational information, make decisions, and take actions with increasing autonomy.
That means we are moving from protecting systems people operate toward assuring systems that increasingly operate themselves.

And that requires something bigger than cybersecurity alone.
It requires trust architecture.

In this episode, Dr. Rhonda Farrell explores five critical shifts leaders should be preparing for: moving from identity management to agent identity, periodic compliance to continuous assurance, human approval to intelligent guardrails, organizational security to ecosystem trust, and incident response to trust recovery.

The defining leadership question is no longer simply:
“Do we trust our AI?” It is: “Can our ecosystem continuously prove why trust is warranted?”

⚙️ This Week’s Challenge
Choose one AI-enabled workflow and map its trust chain: Human → Data → AI → Decision → Action → System → Outcome → Accountability

Then ask: Where does that chain become invisible?
That invisible point may be tomorrow’s risk.

Cybersecurity protects systems. Governance establishes boundaries. Assurance validates performance. But autonomous trust ecosystems make something even more important possible: responsible autonomy at scale.

The organizations that lead the intelligent era won’t necessarily have the most autonomous technology. They will build ecosystems in which technology, people, partners, governance, and communities can trust one another at scale.

🎥 **Watch on YouTube:** https://youtu.be/cjP0btuUWUo

If you enjoy this content, please Like, Subscribe, and Share to help others prepare for the future of cybersecurity, leadership, and digital transformation.

🔔 New episodes of CSTGIA 2026 are released weekly, exploring the emerging trends, technologies, leadership strategies, and enterprise capabilities shaping the future of cybersecurity and organizational excellence.

name: MoCo Code & Coffee November (@ Bethesda Green)
description:
MoCo Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal, co-working session. We're community-led and community-run by devs, for devs. People of all skill levels are invited. Especially new devs!

Bring a laptop, ideas, and we'll provide the coffee and snacks.

Huge thank you to our new venue sponsor, Bethesda Green. Bethesda Green is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit working to build a more sustainable local economy. As an incubator, connector, and community partner, Bethesda Green supports mission-driven startups through the Innovation Lab, helping social-impact founders grow into thriving, purpose-driven businesses. Consider signing up for their newsletter here: https://bethesdagreen.org/subscribe-to-the-bethesda-green-monthly-newsletter/

**Here's how Code & Coffee works**
At 2:30pm, everyone introduces themselves and briefly mention what brought them to Code & Coffee today (project, homework, networking, etc.)
Round 1:

1. Your name
2. What you're working on
3. What you can help others with

Round 2:

* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

Round 3:

* Community events you wanna plug. If none, that's cool too.

**After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized!**

1. For the rest of the day, folks work on their projects, providing one another with help, and/or socialize. It's fully up to you.

Photos and video will be taken at this event for use in our social media. If you'd rather not appear in any of them, just let us know ahead of time and we'll make sure to keep you out of the shots.

**Location**
We will be at Bethesda Green. This location is on the second floor of the Capital One Building. Enter the main building as if you are headed to Capital One, then go up the stairs to your right.
PLEASE NOTE: There is no working elevator at this time, stairs only.

4825 Cordell Avenue, Suite 200
Bethesda, Maryland 20814

More details about finding the space here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bCMFlDXsPerKpshNFZa6b7AsOveYw-ol4cjT5brEadw/edit?usp=

The event will be held in the conference room and shared workspaces of Bethesda Green. Light refreshments (coffee and tea) and snacks will be provided.

**Parking**

* Participants may park on the street or in nearby parking garages.

**Public transit**

* Located near near the **Bethesda** metro station (Red Line).

description: This in-depth lecture and hands-on laboratory workshop (wet lab & in silica) is ideal for those research and bench scientists who are interested in a comprehensive introduction to single cell RNA-Seq. name: Tame PyTorch Recompiles & Unlock Jev GPU Throughput with Zymtrace
description:
**Monday, November 16, 2026 · 9:00–10:00 AM PST · Online**
**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
Join us for two deep dives into hidden AI performance costs: surprise PyTorch recompilations during inference and compute, memory, and communication bottlenecks in Jev training.
**Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth
**Talk #1: Overcoming the PyTorch Recompilation Dilemma in Real-Time Inference Workloads**
by Chaim Rand
`torch.compile` can accelerate steady-state inference, yet a guard failure on a new input shape or layout can trigger an expensive recompilation in the request path. Drawing on his latest post, Chaim will compare six approaches using a dynamic graph-neural-network example: cache preloading, bounded recompilation with eager fallback, Dynamo and input-layout tuning, warmup seeding, background compilation, and ahead-of-time compilation with `torch.export` and AOTInductor. He’ll explain their tradeoffs and how the right choice depends on the model, input distribution, runtime environment, and latency requirements.
**Bio:** Chaim Rand is a machine-learning algorithm developer who writes about PyTorch and practical AI/ML performance optimization.
**Based on:** [Overcoming the PyTorch Recompilation Dilemma in Real-Time Inference Workloads](https://chaimrand.medium.com/overcoming-the-pytorch-recompilation-dilemma-in-real-time-inference-workloads-069fac5485cd)
**Talk #2: From Profiles to Throughput: How TypeSafe Optimized Jev with Zymtrace**
by Israel Ogbole, Co-founder and CEO of Zymtrace
Israel will explore the latest Zymtrace/TypeSafe case study on training and serving Jev. He’ll discuss how continuous CPU/GPU profiling and MCP-accessible profile data supported an iterative optimization loop across compute, memory, communication, and inference synchronization. The published case study reports approximately 46% higher training throughput on the same hardware after three successive changes, plus approximately 10% better inference performance after removing a hidden device-to-host synchronization. The talk will focus on how the team found each bottleneck, measured each change, and identified the next constraint.
**Bio:** Israel Ogbole is co-founder and CEO of Zymtrace, which develops continuous CPU/GPU profiling tools for performance optimization.
**Based on:** [How TypeSafe achieved 46% higher GPU throughput training Jev — with the help of Zymtrace](https://zymtrace.com/article/typesafe-zymtrace/)
**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
**Related Links**
Github Repo: [http://github.com/cfregly/ai-performance-engineering/](http://github.com/cfregly/ai-performance-engineering/)

name: Co-Forward MD
description:
Volunteers are invited to join our open co-working sessions to work on projects, brainstorm ideas, and build community. Come as you are for some or all!

This is styled after the Code for America model. Just show up. We have a backlog of items. Join a team, or propose a new project for Maryland that you've always been dreaming of creating!

We will meet online. RSVP for link.

Coders, UX designers, graphic designers, copy writers, project managers, etc. are welcome! Do you want to learn about code, UX, design, PM, etc.? If someone here is willing to teach you, you might get lucky! (But we are all volunteers, so it will depend on the generosity of strangers.)

We'll be online for 2 hours every other week. It usually takes at least an hour get anything substantial done.

Leave when you have to. You can also volunteer for an assignment to work on between meetings.

name: UAS Project Night
description:
Monday evenings, we will be open for Project Night - a night to work on, collaborate on, or brainstorm on whatever projects you're currently working on or interested in.
Don't have a project? Come see what others are working on and get involved or get ideas. If you have an concept for a group project, bring your ideas and seek out others to join you.

Project Night is a great opportunity to make progress on your projects as a regularly scheduled event. Anyone is welcome to work on projects any time the space is open, but a dedicated night--just for this--is really fantastic.

name: Rachel Beanland: "The Half Life"
description:
When twenty-three-year-old Eileen O’Malley meets charismatic naval officer Paul Archer in a Charleston department store, she doesn’t expect to fall so hard, so fast. But Paul is funny and ambitious, and soon, Eileen’s got a ring on her finger and is following him to the tiny, sun-drenched Mediterranean island of La Maddalena, where Paul will be heading up Radiological Controls aboard a submarine tender.

 

In La Maddalena, Eileen joins a makeshift community of navy wives who are hell-bent on making the island feel a little more like home. But for Eileen, whose brother died in Vietnam, home is a loaded word, and as she settles into life on the island—taking Italian lessons and learning to make culurgiones—she begins to love the place for all the ways it is not like where she comes from.

 

Still, it doesn’t take long for Eileen to be confronted with the complexities of being an American abroad. The decision to send nuclear-powered subs into the La Maddalena Archipelago was a contentious one, and the U.S. government is doing whatever it can to ensure that the island—not to mention all of Italy—doesn’t go communist in the next election.

 

When Italian activists and scientists begin to sound the alarm about possible nuclear contamination in the water, the island erupts in a series of protests, made worse by the ongoing mishaps of the U.S. Navy. Soon, Eileen’s marriage falters and her loyalties begin to shift as she is drawn into a web of secrets—and to a local journalist who forces her to imagine a life beyond the one she’s been handed.

 

Atmospheric, sexy, and quietly defiant, The Half Life is a story of love, complicity, and awakening—of one woman forced to choose between loyalty to her husband and country and to the Italian locals who show her the high cost of American exceptionalism.

 

About the Author: 

Rachel Beanland is the author of The House Is on Fire and Florence Adler Swims Forever, which won the National Jewish Book Award for Debut Fiction. She is a graduate of the University of South Carolina and earned her MFA in creative writing from Virginia Commonwealth University. She lives with her family in Richmond, Virginia.

About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
Fall Focus: Starting Strong — School, Service Year & What Comes Next!
Fall is a season of new beginnings! As young people head back to
school, college, training programs, and work — and our newest Maryland Corps / Service Year members begin their year of service —
TouchPoint
threadHOURS
is here to help everyone start strong and stay on track.
Each Wednesday at threadHOURS, young people can get hands-on support navigating the opportunities and challenges that come with a new school or program year. Whether they need help adjusting to a new schedule, staying on top of school or Service Year expectations, connecting to resources, solving a problem before it becomes a barrier, or thinking ahead to their next academic or professional step, threadHOURS is a place to check in, get connected, and keep moving forward.
For our
Maryland Corps / Service Year members
, threadHOURS is also a place to stay connected throughout the year — celebrating wins, troubleshooting challenges at their host sites, accessing additional resources and opportunities, and making sure their year of service is building toward what comes next.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
The beginning of a new school, work, or service year is a great time to reconnect with your young person. Ask what they’re excited about, what feels challenging, and what would help them start the year strong. Come to threadHOURS together to make a plan, tackle a next step, or connect with someone who can help.
You don’t need to have all the answers — showing up, asking questions, and helping your young person navigate the transition is exactly the relational scaffolding they need.

name: WAUUG November
description:
The Washington Area Unity Users Group (WAUUG) is becoming a regular gathering point for the local game-development community.
With the group back in motion, November is about going a little deeper — more conversations about the technology we use, the projects we’re building, the problems we’re solving, and the people we can learn from along the way.
This meetup is open to Unity developers, game developers, artists, designers, students, hobbyists, industry professionals, and anyone interested in interactive development across DC, Maryland, and Northern Virginia.
Expect a casual evening where people can talk tech, exchange ideas, show projects, ask questions, compare workflows, discuss tools, and make connections with others working in the same space.
If you’re building something, bring it. A finished game is great, but so is a rough prototype, an experimental mechanic, a technical problem, a piece of art, a tool, or an idea you haven’t figured out how to build yet.
You do **not** need to be a Unity expert. WAUUG is intended to be useful whether you’re opening Unity for the first time, studying game development, working on an indie project, or building interactive software professionally.
We’re also continuing to develop what WAUUG can become in 2027, including community talks, member demos, workshops, game jams, technical sessions, career discussions, collaborations, and events with people from the broader Unity and game-development ecosystem.
